links.why: The wayyiqtol cl2 continues the narrative line from cl0, the frame 'God said'. cl0 is narrative, not inside the speech, so it is the nearest clause before cl2 that is not inside a speech.
cl1 is the jussive inside God's speech. The wayyiqtol cl2 follows cl0 on the narrative line, so an 'and then' from the speech clause to cl2 is not the sense.
links.category: narrative line skips a speech clause

links.why: 'God said: let there be light.' The speaking clause cl0 has the command as what was said. The content is the imperative group, as the Exo 8:12 convention gives it.

groups.why: The sender is God (w2, Elohim). It takes a singular verb, as a divine name does, and the speech is 'he said God'. The part is the command group, not its clause cl1, because the command sits inside the speech. The text names no addressee for God's fiat, so none is set.
One jussive command, 'let it be light'. The outcome, 'and there was light' (wayyiqtol cl2), is what it brings about, so it is the effect. The builder's role 'part' is not an imperative member.
groups.category: command with its outcome as effect

none_fit.what: A command followed by a plain wayyiqtol report of its outcome, with no pro-form (no כֵּן). fulfils needs the pro-form and result needs a weqatal, so only the imperative effect records this.

cant_tell.what: Whether cl1 and cl2 are an action-state group (a command, then the same act reported as having happened) rather than an imperative group with an effect.
cant_tell.why: The same two clauses fit both kinds. Kept as an imperative with an effect, since the Hebrew gives one command and its outcome.
